attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps the 'over a trillion dollars' threshold, the present-tense snapshot and the funding-plan clause. Leaving out the aside about forecast losses doesn't change what he committed to. It is an unhedged claim about the present.

contract.note: The plain reading of 'on the hook' as commitments attributable to OpenAI, without double counting, is an ordinary reading and not stretched either way. The result still depends on how partner-financed and conditional plans are attributed, which the speaker did not specify.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure of an Oracle partnership worth over $300B across five years, inside Stargate. It is one part of the total. It does not give OpenAI's full commitments or show whether they pass $1T.
A letter of intent with Nvidia for 10 GW plus a planned Nvidia investment of up to $100B. It gives no priced OpenAI obligation and no funding plan, so it does not settle either part of the claim.

Describes Stargate as a separate company with several funders, with SoftBank responsible for financing. This argues against assigning the whole $500B to OpenAI, but it sets no upper limit on OpenAI's commitments.

reviews.rationale: The packet has partial company disclosures only: Oracle at over $300B, an Nvidia letter of intent, and the Stargate structure. Nothing reconciles OpenAI's own commitments as of 2025-09-29 without overlap, so the evidence neither confirms more than $1T nor sets an upper limit. The contract says partial disclosures cannot set an upper limit. No evidence shows whether a specified funding plan existed. The claim stays unresolved.
